reason: The X button at the bottom right of the Try out Mercury panel has an empty accessible name (probe-52b99e7cbd6e). It holds only an aria-hidden icon, has no aria-label or title, and hover shows no tooltip. Enter closes the panel and turns the button into a map icon that reopens it, so this unnamed button is the only way to reopen the panel. 4.1.2 fails; the panel is optional demo onboarding, so the default medium stands.

The chevron button in the Try out Mercury for yourself header has an empty accessible name (probe-cc54c0dace99). It holds only an aria-hidden icon and has no aria-label or title. Enter on it collapses the panel. Clicking the heading text does nothing, so no labeled control does the same job. 4.1.2 fails; the panel is optional demo onboarding, so the default medium stands.

The Startup chip is a span with role=button and tabindex=0 in a four-chip group that works as a single-select: Enter or Space on a chip swaps the suggestion list below it. Startup is the selected chip on load, drawn with a light-blue fill. Neither aria-pressed, aria-selected nor aria-current is set on any chip, so a screen reader announces all four as plain buttons and the selected industry shows only as a fill, which fails 4.1.2. The list below updates and every chip stays operable, so the impact is friction. Rated low, down from medium.
